title: Whole Arched-Stalk Bilateral-Lip Orchid
description: One complete newly authored stylised above-ground orchid-like plant. Two thick arching basal strap leaves and a small finite crown support one continuous curved flowering stalk. A single bilateral flower carries three tapered sepals, two much broader upper-side petals, a genuinely thick concave flared lower lip with raised side margins, and a short central column. New entire lamina and lip construction, not a sunflower radial disc with a changed petal count, not the old open spathe rolled around a spadix. The asymmetric top/bottom flower organisation and projecting cup-like lip are the identifying structure; no copied old visible meshes. One static whole plant, zero scenes. No exact species, reproductive microanatomy, roots, pollination, growth, cultivation, medicinal or ecological claims.
